environment: Locally built Vue bundle, loopback-only Node API fixture with three synthetic users and one synthetic audit event, Chrome extension browser at 884x448 CSS px; IAB unavailable for this run; no production data or real API

checks.name: baseline_repeated_names
checks.detail: The first focused contract test failed because all blocked checkboxes and row Save/Reset buttons repeated the same accessible name, unlike the account-specific role selectors.

checks.name: baseline_save_focus
checks.detail: On the built bundle before the focus fix, keyboard role change, checkbox Space and Save Enter returned success, but focus fell from the disabled Save button to AXWebArea/body.

checks.name: repeated_row_controls
checks.detail: The accessibility tree exposed distinct role, blocked, Save and Reset names for admin_fixture, alpha_fixture and beta_fixture. Tab from the admin h1 reached section tabs, Refresh, scrollable table, then each row control in order.

checks.name: save_focus_restoration
checks.detail: On the rebuilt bundle, keyboard End selected Administrator for beta_fixture, Space checked blocked, Tab focused its Save button and Enter submitted the local fixture PATCH. Success appeared and focus remained on 'Сохранить изменения для beta_fixture'. A helper test also rejects focus restoration if focus moved elsewhere or the control unmounted.

checks.name: audit_keyboard
checks.detail: The Audit tab opened a labelled section with a content list. Tab from the selected tab reached Refresh; the synthetic event was visible.

checks.name: native_frontend_validation
checks.detail: Full Vitest 186 files and 541 tests PASS; vue-tsc and Vite build PASS. AdminMembersSection 65 lines, focus helper 15 lines, focused specs 13 and 30 lines.

not_run: Real PostgreSQL/Go administration and audit authorization; this browser pass used a synthetic API fixture
Full admin keyboard traversal and trusted release bundle acceptance
observed_follow_up: The Audit list still exposes raw ACCOUNT_ADMIN_STATE_UPDATED and opaque actor/target IDs rather than a localized event description; this needs a separate design leaf.
